text:
maria: Quick flag — infra/runtime team is adding a small set of per-route metrics for quota + latency insights. Need to lock down names, labels, and owners before we ship any instrumentation. Can folks chime in on safe label sets (no user_id!), OTel attributes, and who'll own dashboards/alerts?

devon: +1. Proposed metric names and types:
```
# counters
rw_runtime_route_requests_total{service,region,model,route_id,tier}
rw_runtime_route_tokens_total{service,region,model,route_id,tier}
# histogram for latency (Prom)
rw_runtime_route_latency_seconds_bucket{service,region,model,route_id,tier,le}
# gauge for cache
rw_runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio{service,region,model}
```
Keeping labels to service/region/model/route_id/tier. Avoid user/account IDs in metrics.

ali: Quick note on OTel: make sure we populate common resource attributes: `service.name`, `service.instance.id` (or pod), `deployment.environment`, and `telemetry.sdk.version`. For model naming, I'd prefer `model_variant` (e.g., `gptx-8k-quantized`) instead of a freeform `model` string — that helps grouping. Also confirm exemplar support: attach `trace_id` exemplars to latency histogram buckets.

james: Console/dashboard ask: we need a tenant-aware quota view (per-tenant tokens used vs committed) but we should NOT add `account_id` label to high-cardinality metrics. Proposal: emit low-cardinality `tier` label (free/dev/paid/enterprise) and export a separate per-tenant aggregated metric via the billing pipeline (kafka -> agg -> prom_remote_write). That keeps runtime metric cardinality safe while enabling per-tenant dashboards.

maya: Two things: 1) cardinality thresholds — route_id cardinality estimate? If we have ~300 routes, `route_id` is OK. If >1k it's dangerous. 2) Buckets for latency histogram: use [0.005,0.02,0.05,0.2,0.5,1,2,5] seconds to capture both fast cached responses and slow fallbacks. Add an alert if label cardinality for any metric grows >2x in a week.

observability-bot: Notice: `rw_runtime_route_latency_seconds` (old name) is scheduled for deprecation on 2026-06-01. New names recommended as posted above.

devon: I can own the runtime PRs (instrumentation + tests) for route metrics. Will add safe-default label filter to drop any accidental high-card labels (e.g., endpoint_path, user_id).

ali: I will update the OTel SDK patch and add exemplar wiring + resource attributes. Will also add a mapping for `model_variant` normalization (strip build id suffixes).

james: I'll draft the dashboard template (per-tier and global views) and a companion runbook describing where to get per-tenant numbers (billing-agg pipeline).

maria: Owners noted: devon (runtime metrics PR), ali (OTel/SDK + exemplar), james (dashboard + runbook), maya (cardinality guard checks). Next steps:
- devon: open PR by EOD 2026-03-28 with metrics + unit tests.
- ali: SDK patch by 2026-03-30.
- james: draft dashboard by 2026-04-02.
- maya: run the cardinality scan job on the new metric names after staging deploy and report anomalies.

maria: Also, let's standardize the label naming convention in this case: use lowercase snake_case, prefix runtime metrics with `rw_runtime_`, and avoid embedding region or env in metric name. Use labels for region/env. If anyone objects, speak now or comment on the PR. :thumbsup:

devon: copy, will include test that asserts label set == [service,region,model_variant,route_id,tier].

ali: I'll add unit tests for exemplar presence and resource attributes too.

maria: Thanks all — I'll follow up in the PR thread and tag the `observability` on the final roll.
